mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% q/q over last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises >0.25% q/q.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 6.5% for three consecutive months indicates an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 6.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent and sustained decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and new home sales (HOUST) over two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline q/q for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 1% for three consecutive months signals a supply-side expansion, which typically boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO is above its 12-month MA by >1% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 200,000 persons per month for two consecutive months, combined with a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a tight labor market that elevates wage growth and cost pressures, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200000 for 2 consecutive months AND UNRATE declines in same period
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both PAYEMS > 200000 for two months and UNRATE declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 1.5% for four consecutive months, coupled with a flat or declining GDP (GDPC1), signals weak inflation and sluggish growth, which historically coincides with lower discount rates and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 1.5% for 4 consecutive months AND GDPC1 flat or declining
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive under the specified CPI/GDP conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) that remains below 1% for more than six months in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for >6 months AND CPIAUCSL inflation < 2%
regime_hint: prolonged monetary accommodation with low inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS < 1% for >6 months and inflation < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and persistent rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above their respective 12-month moving averages by at least 1.5% for three consecutive months signals robust supply and demand expansion, which typically boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-mo MA by >1.5% AND GDPC1 > 12-mo MA by >1.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both INDPRO and GDPC1 exceed their 12-mo MA by >1.5% for three months.
